title: HMDA home-purchase originations, Hawaii four counties, 2025 vs 2019

source.publisher: Federal Financial Institutions Examination Council (FFIEC) / Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB), HMDA Data Browser API
source.latest_year_available: 2025 (API returned 2025 data; a 2026 request returned HTTP 400, see raw/hmda/probe_2026_15003.json)

edition.2025: Data Browser data for activity year 2025. The 2025 Snapshot National Loan-Level Dataset file on files.ffiec.cfpb.gov carries Last-Modified 2026-06-23 (raw/hmda/snapshot_head_2025.txt), consistent with the Data Browser serving the 2025 snapshot. The API itself does not label the edition.
edition.2019: Data Browser data for activity year 2019. The API does not state whether it serves the snapshot, one-year or three-year edition for 2019; edition differences are typically small but mean counts may not match a specific static file exactly.

source.cross_check_result: Aggregation API county counts (actions_taken=1, loan_purposes=1) sum to the CSV row count in both years (2025: 9,908; 2019: 13,859).
source.raw_dir: raw/hmda/ (MANIFEST.txt lists every file with URL, UTC download time, bytes and sha256)

filters: construction_method = 1 (site-built) AND total_units in {1,2,3,4}; equivalent to derived_dwelling_category = "Single Family (1-4 Units):Site-Built"
universe.included_without_further_filtering: first and subordinate liens, business-purpose loans, open-end lines, the few reverse mortgages; counts for each are reported so users can re-filter
universe.unit_of_observation: one HMDA loan record (not one property sale). A purchase financed with a first mortgage plus a piggyback second appears twice; n_first_lien is the closer proxy for financed purchases. Cash purchases are not in HMDA.

notes: Definitions (HMDA public LAR codes): occupancy_type 1 = principal residence, 2 = second residence, 3 = investment property. "non_owner_occupied" here = occupancy_type 2 or 3 (not the applicant's principal residence); "investment_only_share" = occupancy_type 3 alone.
loan_type 1 = conventional, 2 = FHA, 3 = VA, 4 = USDA Rural Housing Service / Farm Service Agency.

conforming_loan_limit is the FFIEC-derived flag comparing loan_amount with the FHFA conforming loan limit for the county and year: C = conforming, NC = nonconforming (reported here as "jumbo"), U = undetermined, NA = not applicable. The jumbo split is given for all loans and for conventional first-lien loans only; for FHA/VA/USDA loans an NC flag only means the amount exceeds the GSE conforming limit (e.g. large VA loans), not a private jumbo product. County dollar limits are not reproduced here.

Jumbo shares are not like-for-like across years: the conforming limit rose much more between 2019 and 2025 than many loan sizes did, which moves loans from NC to C without any change in the loan itself.

income = gross annual income relied on in the credit decision, in thousands of USD, rounded to the nearest thousand. It is NA when not relied on (e.g. non-natural-person borrowers, some investor and DSCR-style loans). Income NA rose from 275 loans (2019) to 645 (2025) in the four-county universe. Quartiles use all numeric values including zero or negative incomes; median_excluding_le_zero is also given.

loan_amount and property_value in the public data are the midpoint of the $10,000 interval containing the true value (e.g. 445000 = $440,000 to $449,999). property_value is NA or Exempt (small-filer partial exemption) for some records, and those records are excluded from property-value statistics; n is reported.
Quantile method: linear interpolation between closest ranks (numpy default / Excel PERCENTILE.INC). Medians of even-sized sets can fall between two $10k-interval midpoints.

applicant_age is the primary applicant's age band; 8888 = not applicable (applicant is not a natural person, e.g. an LLC or trust). Shares are given both over all loans (8888 shown as its own category) and over loans with a reported age.
interest_rate_pct_conventional_first_lien.median is an added context metric (median note rate, conventional first-lien purchase loans, Exempt/NA excluded).

Second home vs investment coding moved sharply between years (four-county second-home share 9.1% to 4.9%; investment 12.0% to 16.5%) while the combined non-owner-occupied share was nearly flat (21.2% to 21.3%). The split depends on how lenders classify the loan. The causes were not tested here; possible contributors include the GSE second-home pricing and eligibility changes after 2021 and more business-purpose and DSCR investor lending (business_or_commercial_purpose = 1 in the four-county universe rose from 802 loans, 5.8%, in 2019 to 1,271, 12.9%, in 2025). Use the combined share for trend comparisons.
Maui County 2025 volume (886 loans vs 2,010 in 2019) reflects the post-August-2023 Lahaina wildfire market as well as interest rates. HMDA cannot separate these effects.
Kalawao County (15005) is excluded as requested. No race, ethnicity or sex fields were analyzed or output.

The CSV downloads were filtered server-side to actions_taken=1 and loan_purposes=1. Dwelling-type filtering was done locally, and the drops are reported in filter_funnel (2025: 32 multifamily and 1 manufactured removed; 2019: 61 and 1).
The Data Browser error message for out-of-range years still says "range of 2018-2023", but 2024 and 2025 both returned data. This looks like stale message text.
